assessment: This paper evaluated the lasting effects of acute social isolation on future social interactions in juvenile mice, revealing a compelling oxytocin-mediated mechanism. A clear hypothesis has been laid out within a defined anatomical framework, and social interactions were evaluated using appropriate behavioral paradigms, chemogenetic, and pharmacological tools. The work provides new insights on oxytocin signaling as a key regulator of the neural substrates underlying enduring effects of social interaction.
